title: Pipelines
story: Small tools joined by | do big jobs. This is the shell's superpower.
goal: Read words from standard input, one per line, and print the three most common as COUNT WORD, most common first (ties alphabetical).
hints: uniq -c only counts neighbours, so sort first.
sort -rn puts the biggest count first; head -3 keeps the top three.
sort | uniq -c | sort -k1,1nr -k2 | head -3 | while read -r c w; do echo "$c $w"; done
socratic: Why must you sort before uniq?
Where does each stage's output go?
explain: In one sentence: what did you learn from “Pipelines”?
solution: sort | uniq -c | sort -k1,1nr -k2 | head -3 | while read -r c w; do echo "$c $w"; done
